REGULAR MEETING AGENDA
CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF CERRITOS
AND THE SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE CERRITOS REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY
THURSDAY - JUNE 11, 2015 - CITY HALL -
7:00 P.M.
COUNCIL CHAMBERS, BLOOMFIELD AVENUE AT 183RD STREET
AGENDA MATERIALS: Reports and materials related to items on this Agenda are available for public inspection at the City Clerk's Office, Cerritos City Hall, 18125 Bloomfield Avenue, Cerritos, CA 90703, during normal business hours, 8 a.m. to 5 p.m., Monday through Friday, Telephone (562) 916-1248. Materials submitted to the City Council/Successor Agency after distribution of the agenda packet are available for public inspection in the City Clerk's Office at the above address during normal business hours as noted.
PUBLIC COMMENTS: For all Agenda Items, except for Consent Calendar Items, public comments will be allowed at the time each matter comes up for discussion. Please complete and submit a blue Speaker's Card to ensure that you are recognized when the Agenda item is considered. The general public comments portion of the meeting, under Agenda Item 6, will not exceed 45 minutes, and no speaker will be allowed more than five minutes, unless determined appropriate by the Chair. To assist in the preparation of appropriate responses, persons are requested, but not required, to state their name and city of residence for the record.
PUBLIC HEARINGS: Public hearings will be conducted in the order indicated on the agenda, unless otherwise directed. Please complete and submit a blue Speakers Card if you wish to present testimony. Conduct of public hearings will occur in substantially the following sequence: the item to be heard is announced, a report of written correspondence and staff report are received, and the City Council asks questions of staff. The public hearing is opened and verbal testimony will occur in the following order: the applicant, if applicable, those in favor, opposed, or interested parties, and rebuttal by applicant. Speakers are requested, but not required, to state their name and city of residence for the record. After verbal testimony, the public hearing is closed and the matter is deliberated with a determination being made or a continuation of the matter.

1.  Call to Order

3.  Pledge of Allegiance

  2nd Lieutenant Ryan J. Poblete (The United States Naval Academy Graduation)

  (2015 California Blue Ribbon Schools)

  Whitney High School Robotics Club FIRST Tech Challenge Team (FIRST Tech
  Challenge Robotics World Championships Rockwell Collins Design Innovation Award
  Nomination)

6.  Public Comments and Suggestions

  John Strand spoke regarding the City's water conservation measures.

  James Han spoke regarding curbside house number painting.

  Paul Bellenbaum spoke regarding property valuation in the City.

9.  New and Old Business

9A.  Review and consideration to waive reading of and adopt a RESOLUTION OF THE CITY
  COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF CERRITOS IMPLEMENTING EMERGENCY WATER
  CONSERVATION REGULATIONS (COUNCIL).

  A staff report was given by Vince Brar, Senior Assistant City Manager.

  The Mayor opened public comments.

  David Paquette spoke regarding the emergency water conservation regulations.

  Noting there were no individuals who elected to speak, the Mayor closed public
  comments.

  MOTION: It was moved by Edwards, and seconded by Solanki, to waive full reading of
  and adopt Resolution No. 2015-16, a RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF
  THE CITY OF CERRITOS IMPLEMENTING EMERGENCY WATER CONSERVATION
  REGULATIONS (COUNCIL), subject to the following amendments:

  Section 2. Residential and commercial landscape areas shall be watered between
  the hours of 5 p.m. and 9 a.m. for no more than ten (10) minutes per station.
  Watering shall be limited to two (2) times per week during the months of June
  through September, and one (1) time per week during the months of October
  through May. Residential water customers of the City of Cerritos with even
  numbered addresses are restricted to irrigating only on Mondays and Thursdays
  while those with odd numbered addresses are restricted to irrigating only on
  Tuesdays and Fridays. Landscape irrigation for commercial nurseries and growers,
  fire and erosion protection, the protection of endangered species, environmental
  mitigation projects, and properties using reclaimed water are exempt from this
  provision. Watering using a handheld container; a hose equipped with a shut off
  nozzle; a drip irrigation system producing no more than two (2) gallons per hour;
  or the use of an irrigation system for short durations to make repairs are also
  exempt from the provision.
 City of Cerritos  June 11, 2015
City Council/Successor Agency  Page 6 of 8

9.  New and Old Business (continued)

9A.  (continued)

  Section 3. Use of a drip irrigation system shall be subject to State mandated
  restrictions; and

  Section 4. Violation of the regulations is an infraction punishable by a fine of up
  to five hundred dollars ($500) per day; and

  Section 5. The emergency regulations will remain in effect until the state
  mandated restrictions expire, at which time the City Council shall review the water
  supply conditions to determine the need for continued mandatory conservation
  measures.

  The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Edwards, Pulido, Solanki, Ray, Chen
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

  frequency drive and pump motor repair at Well C-4 Booster Station Pump No. 3,
  located at 16807 Studebaker Road, Cerritos, California 90703 (COUNCIL).

  A staff report was given by Vince Brar, Senior Assistant City Manager.

  The Mayor opened public comments. Noting there were no individuals who elected to

  MOTION: It was moved by Ray, and seconded by Pulido, to approve the purchase and

  Booster Station, Pump No. 3 to General Pump Company in the amount of $31,091.00
  (COUNCIL). The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Edwards, Pulido, Solanki, Ray, Chen
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

9D.  Review and consideration of an end user agreement and an amendment to the
  construction funding agreement with Forest Lawn Memorial Park for the expansion

  A staff report was given by Kanna Vancheswaran, Assistant City Engineer.

  The Mayor opened public comments. Noting there were no individuals who elected to

  MOTION: It was moved by Pulido, and seconded by Edwards, to:

  1. Approve and authorize the City Manager to execute the End User Agreement with

  provision of recycled water to Forest Lawn, subject to final approval by the City
  Attorney, and
  2. Approve and authorize the City Manager to execute Amendment No. 1 to the
  Construction Funding Agreement with Forest Lawn Memorial park for costs
  associated with the expansion of the Cerritos Recycled Water System (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

10.  Legislative Items

10B.  Review and consideration to support or oppose specific legislation in the State or

 City of Cerritos  June 11, 2015
City Council/Successor Agency  Page 8 of 8

10.  Legislative Items (continued)

10B1. (continued)

  MOTION: It was moved by Ray, and seconded by Solanki, to oppose AB 57 and

  Environment and Telecommunications Committee, Senator Mendoza,
  Assemblymember Garcia, League of California Cities – Sacramento and Los

  The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  ABSENT:  None

  The City Council met in Closed Session to discuss Item 12A on the Closed
